Kansas City, MO: what to know before listing

Kansas City is Missouri's largest city by both population and area, and it spreads across four counties: Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass. The county that holds your parcel determines which recorder files the deed and which collector sends the tax bill. Look up the parcel record before you sign.

Two rivers, the Missouri and the Kansas, join at the city. It was incorporated as the town of Kansas on June 1, 1850, renamed the City of Kansas in 1853, and became Kansas City in 1889. With 314.70 square miles of land, conditions change a lot from a Northland subdivision to a Brookside bungalow to a Crossroads loft.

Housing market figures

Mid-2025 estimates put Kansas City at 521,220 residents, 2.6 percent above the 508,012 counted in April 2020. There are 221,979 households and about 55 percent of homes are owner occupied.

  • Middle home value among owners (2020 to 2024): $242,900
  • Median gross rent: $1,238
  • Median household income: $69,166
  • Average commute: 21.7 minutes

Renters are a large share of the city, so investors and landlords are active buyers, especially for houses with deferred repairs. These are citywide middle values. A house in Brookside or the Northland can sit far from them, so ask for a price opinion tied to the specific block and to recent closed sales.

Neighborhoods, school districts and highways

The city is a patchwork of more than 240 neighborhoods. The Country Club District, south of the Country Club Plaza, includes Sunset Hill and Brookside along Ward Parkway, where large historic homes stand. The River Market is the original neighborhood on the Missouri River, and 18th and Vine, Westport and Crossroads are among the districts that attract urban buyers. The Northland is where population has grown fastest.

Kansas City has no single school district. Fifteen districts serve parts of the city, and Kansas City Public Schools covers the inner core. Families check the district for a street first, so say which one applies whenever you talk price with a buyer.

I-435 rings the whole city, and I-29, I-35, I-49, I-70, I-470, I-635 and I-670 cross it, plus US 24, 40, 50, 56, 69, 71 and 169. Easy access to those routes is a selling point for commuters.

Comparing ways to sell

Most Kansas City owners compare three routes: a standard listing, a private sale, and a direct sale to a cash buyer. Pick the one that matches your timeline. Timelines vary widely by area, so base your choice on the house in front of you.

  • Traditional listing: suits a house in good shape in a district buyers search by name, such as the Plaza area or the Northland. Expect showings, an appraisal and a buyer inspection.
  • Private sale: you handle pricing and paperwork, and the Jackson County recorder will not complete forms for you.
  • Cash buyer: fits inherited, vacant or tenant-occupied houses where repairs or registrations are the obstacle. Get the offer in writing and set it beside a listing estimate.

Transit can help marketing. The KC Streetcar runs from Union Station to the River Market, and Amtrak's Southwest Chief and Missouri River Runner stop in the city. Mention those only when your street actually benefits from them.

Registrations for rented or empty homes

Sellers of rented or empty property in Kansas City often meet three city programs. Each has its own office and calendar, so confirm status before a buyer's title work begins.

City programs for rented or vacant homes
ProgramWhat it requires
Healthy Homes Rental Inspection ProgramAll rental owners register under Ordinance 180248; proof of ownership such as a Closing Disclosure, a photo ID and the fee are required; fees changed January 1, 2026; office at 2400 Troost Ave., Suite 3600, 816-513-6464
Vacant Property RegistrationNon-owner-occupied vacant or foreclosed units register online each year between December 1 and January 31; no fee when on time; $50 late penalty; newly vacant property within 90 days, foreclosed property within 14 days
Short-Term Rental registrationAnnual registration through CompassKC; not transferable to a new owner; fines of $200 to $1,000 for operating without one

One detail helps sellers: the vacant property definition excludes a property that a real estate professional is currently marketing, as long as water service has not been shut off. The next vacant property window opens December 1, 2026.

Code violation appeals

The Property Maintenance Appeals Board hears appeals of Notice and Order citations under Chapter 56 and nuisance orders. An appeal must be filed within 10 calendar days from the date printed on the notice and comes with a non-refundable $50 fee. Hearings are on the second Thursday of each month at 9:30 a.m. at City Hall, 414 E. 12th St., on the eighth floor. If you plan to sell rather than fight a citation, tell any buyer about the open notice up front so it does not surface during title work.

Short-term rentals matter at sale time as well. Non-resident short-term rentals are barred in residentially zoned areas, and the registration stays with you, not the house. If your house was a rental on Airbnb or VRBO, tell buyers that the new owner must start a fresh application.

Recording the deed in Jackson County

For a Kansas City address in Jackson County, deeds are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds at the Jackson County Courthouse, 415 E 12th Street, Room 104, phone 816-881-3191. A second office is in the Historic Truman Courthouse in Independence. Parcels in the Clay, Platte or Cass County portions of the city are recorded by those counties instead.

Expect $23 for the first page of a deed and $3 for every page added. Card payments at the counter carry a 2.75 percent processing fee. Staff review and index what you bring but cannot fill in forms for you. Photocopies are not accepted. RSMo 442.380 calls for recording with the recorder of the county where the land is.

Before you accept an offer

Pull together the parcel record showing the county, any rental or vacant registration receipts, and open code notices. Buyers and title companies will ask for all three. If a buyer will rent the house out, ask whether they know about the Healthy Homes registration, since it applies to every new rental owner. Then compare offers by what you take home after liens, tax proration and recording, not by the headline price alone.

Frequently asked questions

Which county do I deal with if I sell a Kansas City house?

The county where the parcel lies. Kansas City reaches into Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass counties, and each has its own recorder.

Do I have to register an empty Kansas City house?

Yes if it is a vacant or foreclosed unit the owner does not occupy. Register online between December 1 and January 31, with a $50 late penalty after that. A property that a real estate professional is marketing, with the water still on, does not count as vacant.

Can a buyer take over my short-term rental registration?

No. Kansas City registrations are not transferable. The new owner has to apply on their own through CompassKC.

What is the deadline to appeal a Kansas City code violation?

Ten calendar days from the date on the notice. The filing fee is $50 and hearings are held monthly on the second Thursday.

What does the Healthy Homes program ask of rental owners?

Every rental owner must register under Ordinance 180248 with a photo ID, a federal tax ID letter when applicable, the fee, and proof of ownership such as a Closing Disclosure or recorded deed. Call 816-513-6464 for current amounts.

Choosing a selling route in St. Louis

You have three options for a house inside the city: engage a broker, sell it yourself, or deal with an investor who buys for cash and takes the property as it sits. Each ends at the same checkpoint, a Housing Conservation inspection that yields a Certificate of Inspection before another household moves in.

Time is the real tradeoff. A listing draws the largest audience, but it means cleaning, staging and showings while a lender works through the buyer's loan. Investors can frequently close on a day you choose, which suits a vacant house, an inheritance from a relative who lived far away, or a property with a tenant.

  • Broker listing: the largest buyer pool and the slowest clock, with fees written into the listing agreement.
  • Selling by owner: you set the price, run the showings and negotiate, then a title company or attorney closes it.
  • Cash bid: little or no showing activity and a faster closing, at a price that reflects repairs the buyer takes on.

An independent city

St. Louis is an independent city, which means it stands apart from St. Louis County. That separation shapes a sale. The city ordinances, the city Recorder of Deeds and the city Collector of Revenue govern a house inside the limits, while a house across the boundary falls under county and suburban rules.

Mid-2025 estimates put the population at 278,144, down 7.7% from the April 2020 base. Just 45.3% of homes are owner-occupied, which means rentals dominate and plenty of sellers are landlords or heirs. Much of the older stock is brick. Inspectors tend to concentrate on roofs, chimneys and basements in such houses.

The Certificate of Inspection

A sale of an occupied house triggers a new Certificate of Inspection when none has been issued in the prior 12 months. Under Ordinance No. 71835, 100% of the city is a Housing Conservation District, so the rule applies to every address.

The visit is a basic code check of interior and exterior conditions under the International Property Maintenance Code. The city says it is no guarantee or warranty of the building and suggests that purchasers consider a commercial grade inspection of their own. The practical details:

  • Fee: $120.00 to apply, or $200.00 if someone is found living in the dwelling without a current certificate.
  • Timing: the visit can be set for no sooner than 3 business days and no later than 15 days after the application.
  • Utilities: water and electric must be operating on inspection day.
  • Violations: when a certificate issues with violations, the owner gets 30 days to repair, and extensions can be granted for weather or other specific causes.
  • Validity: 12 months. The inspection also sets how many people may live in the unit, and no more than three unrelated persons may share a dwelling.

Apply online through the city permit portal or at City Hall, 1200 Market Street, Room 425. The Building Division answers questions at (314) 622-3313.

Where a St. Louis deed is recorded

City properties record with the City of St. Louis Recorder of Deeds, Land Records Department, located in City Hall at 1200 Market Street, Room 126. The counter serves weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and the land records number is (314) 622-3260. Before signing a contract, use the free online search to see that your own deed, any old mortgage and any lien show up as you expect.

Missouri law lets spouses convey real estate by joint deed (RSMo 442.030). Where the property is held as an estate by the entirety, both spouses are bound by the covenants in the deed, so both sign. An heir selling an inherited house needs to ask the title company what probate papers it requires.

For taxes, the St. Louis Collector of Revenue can tell you the current balance on your parcel, so check before setting a closing date.

Storms, ground and old houses

Spring storms bring high winds, large hail and sometimes tornadoes, which is why roofs, gutters and chimneys get close scrutiny. The area south of downtown has numerous sinkholes and caves, though most caves in the city have been sealed. A cash buyer prices these conditions in directly, while a financed buyer may ask for repairs after a home inspection.

Selling with a tenant or an heir's house

Rentals and inherited houses make up a large part of St. Louis sales, and each has its own wrinkles. With a tenant in the house, read the lease for its end date before you agree to a closing day. The inspection also sets how many people may live in the unit, so a buyer who plans to rent will want a copy of the certificate.

With an inherited house, start by sorting out who has authority to sign. The title company will say which probate papers it needs, and having them early avoids a stall at the last minute. If the house is empty and needs work, an as-is cash sale can skip showings and repairs, though the buyer still has to get the Certificate of Inspection before anyone moves in.

What a seller should do first

Handle paperwork first, then decide how much repair work is worth it.

  • Gather the deed and payoff statements and check them against the Recorder's online search.
  • Learn whether a Certificate of Inspection was issued within the last 12 months, since a recent one may mean no new inspection.
  • Walk the outside for property maintenance violations, because inspectors look at exteriors as well.
  • Keep water and electric on through inspection day.
  • Get a listing estimate, sketch a by-owner plan, request a cash bid, and compare the money you would keep from each.

Do the inspection scheduling early, because the window between application and visit can eat into your timeline. If the house is vacant, damaged or occupied by a tenant, selling as-is for cash can remove several of these steps, although the buyer still needs the Certificate of Inspection before anyone occupies the unit.

Frequently asked questions

Is an inspection required before a St. Louis house changes hands?

For an occupied house, yes. A sale triggers a new Certificate of Inspection if none was issued in the last 12 months. Applying costs $120.00, or $200.00 when people are living there without a current certificate.

How long does a St. Louis Certificate of Inspection last?

It is good for twelve months. Violations noted at issuance must be fixed within 30 days, and extensions are possible for weather or other specific causes.

Does a house in poor shape have to be fixed before it sells in St. Louis?

Not necessarily. The inspection is a basic code check, not a full condition report, and a cash buyer may take the house as it is. Someone still needs the Certificate of Inspection before moving in.

Which office records the deed for a St. Louis sale?

The City of St. Louis Recorder of Deeds, Land Records Department, City Hall Room 126, 1200 Market Street, phone (314) 622-3260. Your closing agent usually arranges the filing.

How many unrelated people can share a St. Louis dwelling?

Three at most. The Housing Conservation inspection also fixes how many people may safely live in the unit, which matters when a rental changes hands.

Your selling choices in Springfield

Three paths are open to a Springfield homeowner: sign with an agent, sell on your own, or accept money from a company that buys for cash. Which one wins depends on the condition of the house, the length of your timeline and the price tag on needed repairs.

Springfield is where Greene County government sits. Its estimated population on July 1, 2025 was 169,847, compared with 159,498 in 2010. Springfield leans toward renting: owners live in just 43.9% of occupied homes, and a typical household has 2.04 people. Expect landlords, heirs of rental properties and investors planning to rent to show up on both sides of many deals.

Four colleges sit in and around downtown: Missouri State, Drury, Evangel and Ozarks Technical Community College. A house close to a campus can attract someone planning a rental, so give the distance in your description. Rental registration and short-term rules

West Central, the neighborhood between Chestnut Expressway, Grand Street, Kimbrough Avenue and Kansas Expressway, is the site of a city pilot for rental registration and inspection. Stays of fewer than 30 consecutive days are short-term rentals, which need city registration and a license under City Code Section 36-473. In single-family and townhouse zones, Type 2 rentals need a permit and a neighborhood meeting. Type 3 rentals can have no more than two dwelling units per premise.

Utilities at closing

City Utilities is owned by the city and provides electricity, natural gas, water, telecommunications and transit to roughly 115,000 electric, 84,000 gas and 83,000 water customers. A single provider keeps the handoff at closing simple.

Book a final reading for your closing date so the new owner can start service that day and your account closes cleanly.

Greene County taxes and recording

Property tax in Greene County is billed and collected by the Collector of Revenue, working from values the Assessor sets each January 1. The counter is open on weekdays, 8:00 to 4:30. The office closes on Thanksgiving Day, November 26, and the day after, November 27. For the amount owed on your parcel, phone 417-868-4036.

The Greene County Recorder files deeds. A real estate document costs $26.00 for the first page and $3.00 for each added one, plus a prepaid return envelope. Before mailing anything, phone to verify today's amount.

Normally the title company records the deed and pays tax owed from the proceeds. When closing falls near year end, get your parcel's balance from the Collector first so the settlement statement holds no surprises.

A few weeks of preparation pay off. Start by ordering the paperwork a buyer's lender and title company will want: the deed, a mortgage payoff statement, the latest tax bill and any receipts for roof, heating or plumbing work. Not every Springfield house needs these papers, but a few do. If your house is in the West Central area or has hosted short-term guests, gather the registration or license papers too. Missing paperwork is a common reason closings slip, and it is an easy problem to avoid.

Timing and price

Pick your timeline before you pick a route. Write down the date you need the money, the date you must leave and what the house costs you each month in loan payments, tax and utilities. A cash offer that closes quickly may be worth a lower price when those monthly costs are high, while a patient seller with low costs can afford to wait for a lister's price.

Get at least two opinions on value. An agent can run recent sales near your address, and a cash buyer will give a number based on repairs. Seeing both lets you judge whether the gap is fair.

Selling a Springfield rental

Landlords have extra homework. Begin with the lease, since its end date, the rent and the deposit all matter to a buyer. Once a contract is signed, notify the tenant in writing, and settle early whether the buyer wants the house occupied or vacant.

An investor will weigh rent against price, so a tidy ledger and last year's repair list help. Someone buying to live there cares more about condition and schools. Deciding which buyer you want points you toward listing, selling directly or inviting cash bids.

Cash sales follow a short script: a written offer, a title search for liens and back taxes, signatures on the deed and settlement papers, and payment once the deed is recorded. Columbia housing and who owns homes

Columbia is the seat of Boone County in central Missouri, about 120 miles from both St. Louis and Kansas City. Population was estimated at 130,851 on July 1, 2025. Almost all of the city is in Columbia Public Schools, whose four high schools are Hickman, Rock Bridge, Muriel Battle and Frederick Douglass. A very small part of the city is in the Hallsville R-IV district.

Every rental unit in Columbia needs a Certificate of Compliance, and it is unlawful to operate a rental without a current one. A buyer of a former rental will want to know the certificate is valid.

City offices and programs

The city's Housing and Neighborhood Services department runs several programs that touch a house sale. Its Office of Neighborhood Services handles code enforcement at 573-817-5050, and the Housing Programs Division at 573-874-6321 runs federal and local housing aid.

Boone County property taxes at a sale

The Boone County Collector mails tax statements in November, and real estate tax is due upon receipt but no later than December 31.

The tax stays attached to the property as a lien, so a new owner is liable for any unpaid amount. Buyer and seller usually prorate the year, and the buyer is credited at closing for the months the seller owned the house. No money is paid to the collector at the sale itself. A closing on or after October 1 can leave the bill in your name, so give the collector the new owner's name and address.

The assessor values a house at 19 percent of its market value for tax purposes. Delinquent parcels may go to a public tax certificate sale on the fourth Monday in August. Boone County also has a Senior Real Estate Tax Relief Program for approved primary residences.

Selling a former rental step by step

If the house has been leased, work through the city side before you talk price. First, find out whether the Certificate of Compliance is current, because operating without one is unlawful. Afterward, the deed is filed at the Government Center on East Walnut, and the Assessor updates the boundary maps from warranty deeds the recorder receives.

Deeds for Columbia addresses are filed at the Boone County Government Center, 801 East Walnut, Room 132, in Columbia. The phone number is 573-886-4345. Property boundary maps are updated by the Assessor's office from warranty deeds the recorder receives.

Preparing a house for inspection

Older Columbia houses with tenants in place or a lapsed rental certificate can be harder to sell on the open market. Before you list, confirm the certificate status with Neighborhood Services, and if the house was a rental, ask what an inspection would look at. A gas appliance needs an HVAC certification before the inspection, so book that visit first and keep the certification paperwork for the file.

Buyers' inspectors in Columbia will also look hard at air conditioning, attic ventilation, roofs, gutters and older plumbing. Service the equipment and keep the receipts, because a seller who can show maintenance records usually gets fewer repair requests.

In Columbia you can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept an investor's as-is offer. Because tenants or a lapsed certificate make a listing harder, owners of those houses often look at a direct purchase.

Gather your payoff letter, Boone County tax statement, rental certificate status and school district first. That packet lets you compare a listing's net proceeds against a cash offer without delay. Yes. The city allows transfer within 90 days of title transfer for a $15 fee, and the certificate keeps its unexpired term. Call Neighborhood Services at 573-817-5050 to arrange it.

When are Boone County property taxes due?

Upon receipt of the bill, and no later than December 31. The Collector mails statements in November.

Who pays the property tax at closing?

Taxes are generally prorated, with the buyer credited by the seller for the months the seller owned the house. No tax money is paid to the collector's office at closing.

Where is the Boone County Recorder of Deeds?

At the Boone County Government Center, 801 East Walnut, Room 132 in Columbia. Call 573-886-4345 with questions about copies or filings.

Which school district serves my Columbia house?

Almost all of the city is in Columbia Public Schools, and a very small part lies in the Hallsville R-IV district. Check the district boundary for your address.

Independence at a glance

Harry Truman grew up here, and the Truman Library and Museum and the Truman National Historic Site are in town.

The 2020 census counted 123,011 residents, making it the fifth-largest city in Missouri. Most of the city is in Jackson County, and a small part extends into Clay County. ZIP codes run from 64050 through 64058.

Rental Ready program for landlords

Every residential rental unit in Independence needs a city license and must pass an inspection before it can be leased. The Rental Ready program started June 1, 2017. The council expanded it in January 2025 from nine inspection items to sixteen, and the new rules took effect May 1, 2025.

Recording a deed at the Jackson County Recorder of Deeds starts at $23 for page one. Estate sellers often need a certified death certificate copy, which is $20. A state or federal tax lien is $3. Independence falls within four public school districts: Independence, Blue Springs, Fort Osage and Raytown. Which district your street belongs to matters to buyers, so confirm it before you list. Independence has three public high schools and four public middle schools, among them Bridger, Pioneer Ridge, Bingham and Nowlin. Blue River Community College and a Graceland University campus are in the city.

Independence Power and Light, a city-owned electric utility founded in 1901, serves customers in town.

Choosing how to sell

An agent listing fits a house in good repair. A direct cash sale fits a house with deferred work, a tenant, or an estate that needs a quick close, because the buyer takes the house as it stands and you skip showings and repair requests. Get any offer in writing and ask who pays closing costs.

Before you accept, check three things: which county bills your tax, whether a rental license and inspection are current, and whether any code violation is open. Open violations and unpaid tax can slow a closing, so settle them first or tell the buyer up front. The title company handles the payoff, the proration and the deed recording. Bring your latest tax statement, mortgage payoff figure and any rental paperwork to the first conversation so a buyer can price the house quickly.

The city licenses and inspects them. Landlords need a business license and a Rental Ready inspection every two years at $100 per unit. Since January 1, 2026, a valid license is required before utilities can start for a tenant.

Jackson County for most addresses and Clay County for the small portion of the city that extends into it. Check your tax statement to see which collector sent it.

Tall grass over 7 inches, trash containers left at the curb, unlicensed vehicles parked outside and deteriorated fences or sidewalks. Fines for a summons range from $100 to $500.

Can I list my Independence house as a short-term rental?

Only with a city permit approved by the Planning Commission, and no new rental may be within 500 feet of another. Operators remit transient guest tax monthly.

Selling quickly in Lee's Summit

Three paths exist for a Lee's Summit homeowner: hire a listing agent, sell on your own, or take an as-is cash offer. Speed usually comes down to the condition of the house and whether the title is clean.

A well-kept house in an established subdivision can sell on an ordinary listing within a few weeks. A house with a failing roof, a stack of Neighborhood Services notices or a tenant who has stopped answering the door tends to stall once buyers read the inspection report. Ask every buyer for a written offer, then subtract commissions, repairs and carrying costs from the listing estimate to see which route leaves more in your pocket.

About the city

Lee's Summit is a Kansas City suburb in Jackson County, and part of it extends into Cass County. It borders Kansas City on the west and northwest, Independence on the north, and Greenwood and Lake Winnebago to the southeast and south.

The town started in 1865 as Strother, a stop platted along the Missouri Pacific tracks, and took the name Lee's Summit in 1868. Postwar highways and demand for single family homes turned the farm community into a commuter suburb, and the New Longview neighborhood, built in 2004, now covers part of the old Longview Farm estate.

Downtown is a ten-block by ten-block district on the National Register of Historic Places, ringed mostly by single family streets. Interstate 470, U.S. Route 50 and Missouri Route 291 make a triangle of highways around the center, with Route 150 crossing the south side. Six large reservoirs lie in and around the city, among them Longview Lake and Raintree Lake. About 80 percent of residents commuted outside the city as of 2015, so buyers often ask how long the drive to downtown Kansas City or Overland Park will take. For an inherited or vacant house, walk the exterior before you list. Mow, clear trash containers from view and repair fence sections. If you suspect a complaint was filed while you were away, call Development Services at 816.969.1200 and ask whether a case exists on the address.

Short-term rental rules

A rental of this kind needs a business license and belongs inside the Old Town Master Development Plan area, which is east of US Highway 50, west of Route 291 North and south of Chipman Road. Outside Old Town, the parcel must exceed one acre. Only single-family houses and duplexes qualify, and the owner or a local representative has to occupy a unit on the same or an adjacent parcel.

Deeds are filed with the recorder in the parcel's county, and the annual tax bill must be paid by December 31. Because Lee's Summit sits in both Jackson and Cass counties, find out which one holds your parcel before you plan closing.

On page one of a deed, Jackson County's Recorder of Deeds wants the document title, the date, every grantor with marital status, every grantee, any statutory addresses and the legal description, all below a three-inch top margin. Your title company normally prepares and records the deed, but if you write one yourself, copy that layout.

The 2026 real estate and personal property bills went online in Jackson County on November 3, 2026, and are due by December 31, 2026. Houses are assessed at 19 percent of market value. The Collection Department has no authority to reduce an assessment or a levy, so take valuation disputes to the assessor. Your parcel's share in Cass County, if any, is billed by that county's collector.

A handful of problems cause most delays, and you can check for each of them before you pick a buyer.

  • An unresolved Neighborhood Services notice or unpaid mowing charge.
  • An occupant who has not agreed to a move-out date.
  • Structural or water problems that an inspector will flag.

Knowing which apply lets you set a realistic closing date. Buyers who purchase as-is, including cash buyers, are often more comfortable taking on several of these than a buyer who relies on a mortgage appraisal.

No. A notice from Neighborhood Services does not bar a sale, though buyers will ask about it. The city typically gives 10 days to correct a violation, so a quick cleanup often closes the case. Development Services at 816.969.1200 can tell you whether a case is open.

Do I record my deed in Jackson County or Cass County?

It depends on the parcel. Most of the city lies in Jackson County, yet a portion extends into Cass County. Your title company or the county assessor can confirm where your address falls.

What is the deadline for the 2026 property tax bill on a Jackson County home?

December 31, 2026. Jackson County put the bills online on November 3, 2026. Your closing agent can show how the year's tax will be divided with the buyer.

Only in the Old Town Master Development Plan area or on a parcel larger than one acre, and only in a single-family house or duplex. A business license is required, and the owner or a local representative must live on the same or an adjacent parcel.

Permits and inspections

The Building Division works from the second floor of City Hall, 100 North Main Street, and its main line is 636-379-5660. The Recorder of Deeds

The Recorder of Deeds keeps the county's public land records, including deeds and tax liens. After closing, the title company or attorney sends the signed deed there, so most sellers never visit.

Recorded deeds show up in the office's land index. If you ever want proof that a lien was released or a deed reached the record, ask the Recorder. The office also holds federal and state tax liens and marriage records.

The posted fee schedule is dated August 28, 2022, so phone the office for the present per-page rate before you pay anything yourself. A document that is not on a standard form carries an added charge.

Written answers let you stack two or three offers side by side. Keep your permit papers, the latest tax bill and any homeowners association paperwork on hand so the buyer's side never waits on you.

A cash closing usually moves like this: you accept an offer, the title company searches the record for liens, you sign the deed and a settlement statement, and funds are released once the deed is recorded. Occupancy permit rules

Mail Clay County tax so it is postmarked by December 31. Late payments draw a one-time 9 percent penalty and 1.5 percent interest each month.

You owe a one-time 9 percent penalty and 1.5 percent monthly interest on what is unpaid. Anything postmarked after December 31 is late.

Your selling options in Nixa

There are three ordinary routes in Nixa: list with an agent, handle the sale yourself, or accept a cash offer. A cash buyer is usually the fastest answer for a house with deferred work. A listing usually wins the best price when the house is in good shape. A buyer who means to rent the place will also run into the city's rental inspection after closing.

Nixa grew quickly, from 12,124 residents in 2000 to 23,257 in 2020, and many of today's streets were built in that burst. Plenty of similar houses means an ordinary one competes on price and condition. If yours is a tired rental, an empty house or an inheritance, an as-is buyer will take on the repairs and spare you the open houses.

  • Agent listing: the widest audience, plus cleaning, staging and weeks of waiting on the buyer's loan.
  • Owner sale: no agent fee, but pricing, showings and the contract land on you.
  • Cash purchase: no repairs requested, and you choose the day you hand over keys.

Whatever route you lean toward, compare the check you would actually receive once repairs, fees and monthly carrying costs are subtracted.

Nixa housing figures

The 2020 census counted 23,257 people in Nixa, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,597, which is 14.4 percent above the 2020 base. The city is in Christian County, a short drive south of Springfield.

Nixa population and housing, 2020 to 2024 estimates

Children make up 27.6 percent of residents, so a family-sized house with a yard near an elementary school has an easy audience. Put the school name in your listing, because young families search that way. Another number: 91.7 percent of residents lived at the same address a year before, which tells you owners rarely leave and inventory stays thin. A fairly priced listing can stand out in that setting.

Nixa's rental inspection rule

Under city rules, a rental unit at least a year old must clear an inspection before each new tenant moves in and before utilities can be put in the tenant's name. You only feel this rule if your buyer plans to rent the property, though any investor will ask about it.

  • Fee: $25 per inspection, paid before the visit through a link the city emails after you submit the request form.
  • Notice: give 24 hours, because same-day visits are not offered. Weekday slots run from 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., booked as a morning or afternoon window.
  • Who can schedule: only a landlord or property manager.
  • Penalty: $50 when a tenant moves in or gets keys ahead of a cleared inspection. An early move-in inspection costs $75.
  • Failed inspection: you get 90 days to repair and ask for a re-inspection. Later than that, a fresh inspection and another $25 apply.

Have the house empty, clean and ready to occupy. The inspector checks the roof and gutters, smoke detectors on every story, GFCI protection in bathrooms, water heater safety valves, the windows and doors, weeds above 12 inches and other items on the city's checklist. Planning and Development answers questions at (417) 725-5850.

Short-term rentals

The city code covers short-term residential rentals, and the text was reworked after Missouri House Bill 1662 took effect in June 2022. Phone Planning and Development to learn which version governs before you advertise nightly stays or sell to someone who wants them.

An ordinance from August 2019 first allowed these stays, but only inside a primary residence and only with a special use permit. A May 2024 staff proposal created two categories. Renting out the home you live in needs just a city business license. Renting a second property would bring a ban on accessory structures, a yearly rental inspection and a 150-foot gap from other short-term rentals. Anyone buying an Airbnb house should ask whether the proposal was adopted as written.

Utilities and moving day

A new owner opens a utilities account directly with Nixa Utilities. Expect to supply a residential application, photo ID, information on each adult in the home and a deposit. A rental also needs the cleared inspection described above before service goes into a tenant's name.

On your side, request a final meter reading dated to closing so the account changes hands that day and your bills end.

Christian County records and taxes

Land records for the county sit with the Recorder of Deeds, whose office is in the Historical Courthouse at 100 W. Church Street, Room 104, in Ozark. Your title company normally files the deed once the sale closes, so a visit is rarely needed.

Filings arrive by walk-in, mail or electronically, and eRecording runs through vendors such as iCounty Technologies. Staff will not provide forms, notarize or offer legal advice. Missouri Senate Bill 938 changed recording fees at the end of August 2026, so ask the office what a recording costs today. A free service at deedwatch.com emails an owner whenever a paper is recorded under a registered name, a low-cost guard against deed fraud.

Residential assessments are set at 19 percent of market value. The levy is built from thirteen school districts, eight road districts, ten cities, nine fire districts and other bodies, so the districts covering your address decide the bill. The Collector's Office in Room 101 of the courthouse can give you the balance and due date. Whatever is owed gets settled at the closing table.

Older owners have a credit to consider. The county's Senior Citizen Real Estate Tax Credit is open to owners who are at least 62 by December 31, 2026, have lived in the home since at least June 29, 2026 and have paid their 2026 taxes. First-time applications run from March 1, 2027 to June 15, 2027, which may matter if you are weighing a sale against staying.

Preparing for offers

  1. Gather your deed, a mortgage payoff statement and the newest tax bill.
  2. Note whether a tenant lives there and whether the rental inspection is done.
  3. Get every offer in writing with a price, a closing date and the party responsible for title and recording costs.
  4. Line the offers up by net proceeds, after repairs, commissions and carrying costs.
  5. Schedule the last utility reading for closing day.

Seeing two or three bids on one page makes the speed-versus-price tradeoff much plainer.

Frequently asked questions

Is a house inspected by the city when it sells in Nixa?

Only when the buyer will rent it out. The city's program covers rental units before each new tenant arrives, at $25 per inspection, and a landlord cannot place a tenant until the unit clears.

What happens if a tenant moves into a Nixa rental early?

The penalty is $50, and an early move-in inspection costs $75. A landlord with repeat violations can be summoned to Municipal Court.

Where do I record a deed for a house in Nixa?

With the Christian County Recorder of Deeds, Historical Courthouse, 100 W. Church Street, Room 104, Ozark. The title company handling your closing can file it.

Can I run an Airbnb in my Nixa house?

Possibly. The short-term rental rules were rewritten after Missouri House Bill 1662. Renting your own primary residence needs a city business license, while other houses may face a yearly inspection and 150-foot spacing. Ask Planning and Development for the current text.

How do I set up utilities after buying a house in Nixa?

The buyer applies at Nixa Utilities, 715 W Mt Vernon St, with a residential application, photo ID, details on every adult in the home and a deposit. A rental also needs a cleared rental inspection.

What speeds up or slows down a Belton sale

A Belton owner has three paths: list with an agent, sell alone, or accept a cash offer. The house's condition and whether tenants live in it usually settle the choice. The city's rental program, plus Cass County's role in tax and recording, shape the calendar, so line those pieces up early.

Rental houses catch people off guard. Since January 1, 2025, each rental unit inside the city limits must be registered, and the city inspects between tenants. A landlord selling, or a buyer who plans to lease the place out, should read that program before setting a closing date.

Belton at a glance

Belton is in northwestern Cass County, part of the Kansas City metro area, on Missouri Route 58 west of I-49 and U.S. 71. Population was estimated at 26,193 on July 1, 2025, up from 23,953 in 2020. Only 59 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so rentals are common, and an owned home is worth $203,200 at the midpoint. Midpoint gross rent is $1,290.

Belton School District #124 serves most of town, while part of eastern Belton belongs to the Raymore-Peculiar district. Check which one applies to your address, since buyers ask.

Rental registration and code enforcement

All rental units inside Belton must be registered, and inspections happen between tenants, after one leaves and before the next moves in. The program took effect on January 1, 2025, under an ordinance the council approved on October 10, 2023.

Write to rental@belton.org to book an inspection or ask about the program. Neighborhood Improvement and Code Enforcement, a division of Community Development, enforces the property maintenance and use ordinances. Active violations show on the city's eTRAKiT portal, where a public account lets you view them, apply for permits and schedule inspections. Look up your own address there before you take an offer.

Short-term rentals

A short-term rental in Belton needs city approval, and the rules are tight. Under Ordinance 2025-4950, passed November 25, 2025, each one needs a registration plus a special use permit. Fees add up to at least $270 to begin: $70 for annual registration, $50 for inspection and $150 for the permit.

Occupancy is capped at two adults per bedroom plus one more adult per dwelling, with ten guests the ceiling, children included. Hosts remit the city's 5 percent hotel and motel tax monthly, and nobody may register more than five units. Sites are limited to the Old Town Belton area and parcels over three acres, so ask Community Development how the location rule applies to your address.

Operating outside the rules draws fines of $200 to $500, and every day can count as its own offense. A buyer who wants a Belton short-term rental should get the city's answer before closing. If you are selling a house that was run as a short-term rental, tell the buyer up front whether the registration and permit were ever in place, and expect them to ask for proof.

Cass County property taxes when you sell

Cass County bills real estate once a year, in November, and expects payment on receipt and by December 31, judged by U.S. postmark. Penalties and fees can climb to 25 percent in the first delinquent year. Assessment is 19 percent of market value, and the levy is figured per hundred dollars of that assessed amount.

When a house changes hands, the buyer owes the whole bill by December 31. Buyer and seller usually prorate the year between themselves, and the Collector gets no payment at the closing table. The tax is a lien on the parcel, so any unpaid amount passes to a buyer. Unpaid parcels can end up at the yearly tax certificate sale, the fourth Monday of August, at the Harrisonville courthouse.

Should a bill reach you after the sale, send the Collector the new owner's name and address. In Harrisonville, the Collector is at 2725 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8377. The Assessor is next door at 2733 Cantrell Road, 816-380-8400.

Before you list

A short checklist keeps surprises out of the contract period. Belton's own portals and the county offices hold most of what you need.

  • Rental registration and inspection results, if the house has been leased.
  • A look at the eTRAKiT portal for open code violations or permits on the address.
  • The Cass County tax statement and parcel number from the Collector or Assessor.
  • A copy of your deed from the Recorder, plus any release for a paid-off loan.
  • The school district for the address, since eastern Belton can fall in Raymore-Peculiar.

If the house was a rental, get the registration current and the last inspection done before showing it, because the buyer or the next tenant will run into the same program. Sellers with open code violations can often resolve them faster than they can negotiate around them. Walk the property with the portal open, so you can match any permit or violation to what a buyer would see. If something is open, call Community Development before you list, and ask what closes it out.

For the tax side, ask the Collector for the current bill and any delinquent amount, and have the parcel number handy when you call. Then confirm with the title company how they will prorate the year, since the county takes no money at the table. Finally, order a copy of your deed from the Recorder if you cannot find yours, and ask whether any old loan release was ever recorded.

Recording the deed after a Belton sale

Deeds are filed with the Cass County Recorder of Deeds at 102 E. Wall Street in Harrisonville, phone 816-380-8118, open weekdays 8 a.m. until 4 p.m. Staff there will not draft documents, so hire a title company or real estate attorney for that.

Sign up at casscounty.com/fraud for an alert whenever a document is recorded under your name. An unrecorded deed binds only the signers and people with actual notice (RSMo 442.400), which is why closing agents file at once.

A Belton owner short on time because of repairs, tenants, an inherited house or back taxes may find a cash purchase shortens the schedule, with the inspection, tax and recording steps unchanged. A cash buyer still needs the tax payoff and the rental paperwork, so gather those first.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Belton landlord have to register before selling?

Yes, every rental unit inside Belton must be registered, at $20 per unit a year. Inspections happen between tenants, so a vacated rental should pass before the next occupant or buyer moves in.

Is a short-term rental allowed at a Belton house?

Only with registration and a special use permit under Ordinance 2025-4950. The minimum startup cost is $270, and hosts owe the 5 percent hotel and motel tax.

What is the Cass County tax deadline for a Belton house?

Pay on receipt and by December 31. Late payment can bring penalties and fees as high as 25 percent in the first delinquent year.

Who handles the tax bill at a Belton closing?

Buyer and seller generally prorate the taxes, and nothing is paid to the Collector at the sale. The new owner pays the whole bill by December 31.

What is Belton's population?

The 2020 census counted 23,953 and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,193. Belton sits in northwestern Cass County within the Kansas City metro area.
